summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Jean Mathonet, a Belgian footballer born in Bévercé, Malmedy in 1925 and who died in Malmedy in 2004. It highlights his career at Standard Liège, where he was the Belgian First Division's top scorer in 1956, and his national team record of 13 caps between 1952 and 1958, beginning with a debut against France.
one_line: Belgian footballer who was top scorer of the Belgian First Division in 1956 with Standard Liège and played 13 times for Belgium.
key_facts: Jean Mathonet was born on 6 October 1925 in Bévercé, Malmedy.
Jean Mathonet died on 22 October 2004 in Malmedy.
Jean Mathonet was a Belgian football player.
Jean Mathonet finished as top scorer of the Belgian First Division with 26 goals in 1956.
Jean Mathonet scored his 26 First Division goals in 1956 while playing for Standard Liège.
Jean Mathonet played 13 times with the Belgian national team between 1952 and 1958.
Jean Mathonet made his international debut on Christmas 1952.
Jean Mathonet's international debut was a 0–1 friendly win against France.
